_note: Contemporary designers: hand-picked Wikimedia Commons photos (index into commons-candidates.json). Facts come from the Commons file descriptions and the exhibiting museums.

Iris van Herpen.bio: Dutch couturier who builds garments with 3D printing, laser cutting and heat-bonded materials, often with scientists and architects.

Guo Pei.bio: Beijing couturier known for monumental, hand-embroidered gowns that can take thousands of hours to make.

Marine Serre.bio: Paris designer whose collections are built largely from regenerated and upcycled materials.

Alexander McQueen.bio: London designer whose theatrical collections joined Savile Row tailoring with romantic, often dark storytelling.

Viktor & Rolf.bio: Amsterdam duo who treat couture as conceptual art, from upside-down shows to dresses cut like sculptures.

Rei Kawakubo.bio: Founder of Comme des Garçons, who questions what a garment is with abstract, body-reshaping forms.

Yohji Yamamoto.bio: Tokyo designer of asymmetric, mostly black tailoring that drapes away from the body.

Issey Miyake.bio: Designer and engineer of cloth, best known for permanent garment pleating and experiments with new fibres.

Thierry Mugler.bio: Paris designer of sculpted, armour-like silhouettes and some of the most theatrical shows of the 1980s and 90s.

John Galliano.bio: Designer known for historical romance and bias-cut drama, at his own label, Christian Dior and Maison Margiela.

Gareth Pugh.bio: London designer of geometric, often monochrome looks in unexpected materials, from plastic to bin bags.

Hussein Chalayan.bio: Designer who brings furniture, technology and migration into fashion: tables that become skirts, dresses lit by LEDs.

Molly Goddard.bio: London designer of exuberant, hand-smocked tulle dresses.

Vivienne Westwood.bio: From punk to historical tailoring, a designer who reworked British dress history and campaigned on climate.

Shaun Leane.bio: London jeweller trained in traditional goldsmithing, known for sculptural body pieces made with Alexander McQueen.

Kei Ninomiya.bio: Designer of the Noir Kei Ninomiya label, who builds garments from thousands of small parts without sewing them.
